sections.html:
Every deed and similar real estate document in the county goes through the Navajo County Recorder, reachable at 928-524-4194. Walk-in service is in Holbrook, the county seat, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m.

An hour's drive or more separates many sellers from Holbrook, so the Recorder placed two remote kiosks in other towns. Other county numbers you may need are listed after them.

  • Snowflake Justice Court kiosk: 145 South Main Street, Suite D, main lobby, Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Navajo County Health Department kiosk, Show Low: 600 N. 9th Place, main lobby, Monday through Thursday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Assessor: 928-524-4086 for assessment questions.
  • Treasurer: 928-524-4172 for tax bill questions.
  • Clerk of the Superior Court: 928-524-4188 for marriage and divorce records.

Any instrument costs a flat $30 to record, mailed back or filed electronically. For a deed, the Affidavit of Property Value form comes with that price. The schedule leans on A.R.S. 11-475 for amounts and A.R.S. 11-480 for document format.

ServiceNavajo County fee
All instruments$30
Government and state agencies$15
Copies of records, per page$1
Certified copy, per document$3
Survey or plat, first sheet / each additional$24 / $20
Copy of a map, 18 x 24 / 24 x 36 inches$5 / $7

Because the fee is per instrument, a deed plus a separate release or corrective document means more than one $30 charge. Add up what you are recording before you write the check, and ask the title company for a total if several documents are involved.

Break the layout rules and the counter can send your deed back. The county's list, drawn from A.R.S. 11-480, follows.

  • Ten point is the smallest allowed print.
  • Paper can be as wide as 8.5 inches and as long as 14 inches.
  • Leave at least a half inch at the bottom of every page.
  • Keep two inches clear at the top of page one for the stamp and return address.

If you drafted it yourself, measure page one before you set out. A brief title or caption saying what the document is also helps.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and the Affidavit of Property Value
sections.html:
No charge on the county's schedule varies with what you sell for. Under Article 9, Section 24 of the state Constitution, new taxes, fees and stamp requirements on real property sales are off limits, and only charges already existing on December 31, 2007 are excepted.

The state's substitute for a tax is an affidavit. A.R.S. 11-1133 makes both sides sign an Affidavit of Property Value on any deed passing title. An incomplete one, with no exemption noted, must be refused by the recorder. Expect questions on price paid, down payment, financing, parcel number and whether the buyer will live in the home or rent it.

A.R.S. 11-1134 exempts, among others, gifts between close relatives, court-ordered conveyances and trustee's deeds. Name the exemption you rely on right on the deed.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax roll after recording
sections.html:
Recording a deed starts a chain. Ownership records update, then the Navajo County Assessor swaps the owner name on the tax roll, and the new name appears online at the Treasurer's Property Information page one day after that entry.

Buyer and seller don't get separate bills. The tax belongs to the property, so the title company divides it on the settlement statement and credits the buyer with your portion. Read that statement before you close.

Should a bill reach you later, send it along to the new owner, or write sold on the envelope and mail it back to the Treasurer. Manufactured homes never affixed to land are handled differently: after title moves, old and new owners both tell the Assessor, at 928-524-4086.

sections.h2: Liens, titles and copies of a deed
sections.html:
The Recorder's FAQ list covers title searches, liens, a property's selling price, copies of a deed and removing a decedent's name from a deed. Call 928-524-4194 and ask about your own parcel.

A copy is $1 per page, and certification adds $3 per document. If a deceased owner's name is still on the deed, the Recorder files the fix, yet an attorney or title company picks the right paperwork. Ask them first and you'll record once.

Back taxes? The Treasurer's Parcel Information Search shows a balance by parcel number, owner name or address, and the Treasurer answers at 928-524-4172. The Navajo County property tax guide covers due dates and the lien process.

Navajo County had 106,717 residents in 2020 and 56,180 housing units, with 34.4% vacant. About 70.9% of occupied homes had owners living in them. Show Low is the largest city. Across 9,960 square miles, a kiosk stop or a mailed deed often saves a long drive. Whichever route you pick, build in extra days before closing so a rejected document can be fixed and resubmitted without moving your closing date.

sections.h2: Selling here: a practical order of steps
sections.html:
Work through it in this order. One: compare the legal description and owner names on your deed with the last recorded deed. Two: ask the title company whether an exemption fits or the full affidavit is required. Three: sign in front of a notary and confirm page one has its blank top strip. Four: let the title company submit it, or deliver it yourself with $30. Five: request the recorded copy and file it with your closing papers.

Going in person? Bring the signed original, the finished affidavit or your exemption claim, payment for the $30, and a typed return address on the document. Counter staff can point out what's missing but won't say what a deed ought to contain. If something is unclear, phone 928-524-4194 before the trip.

A cash sale follows the same path minus the buyer's lender, so no new loan document is normally recorded. Paying off your own mortgage still requires a release.

For a parcel inside a reservation boundary, ask the Recorder and a title company how the deed has to be recorded before you plan the sale.

faqs.q: What does a Navajo County deed recording cost?
faqs.a: A flat $30 whether the deed comes back by mail or is recorded electronically. Government agencies pay $15, copies run $1 a page and certified copies add $3 per document.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to Holbrook to record a Navajo County deed?
faqs.a: No. Kiosks accept recordings at the Snowflake Justice Court, 145 South Main Street, Suite D (Monday to Friday), and at the Navajo County Health Department, 600 N. 9th Place, Show Low (Monday to Thursday). Both open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell a house in Navajo County?
faqs.a: The county charges nothing tied to the price, and the state Constitution (Article 9, Section 24) blocks new taxes or fees on conveying real property apart from those existing on December 31, 2007. Your deed still needs the Affidavit of Property Value.

faqs.q: How must a Navajo County deed be laid out?
faqs.a: Print at ten point or larger, on pages no bigger than 8.5 by 14 inches, with a half-inch bottom margin and a clear two-inch strip across the top of page one for recording details.

faqs.q: After closing, who updates the owner on the tax roll?
faqs.a: The Navajo County Assessor does, once the deed is recorded, and the Treasurer's Property Information page shows it the next day. Manufactured home title transfers go to the Assessor at 928-524-4086.
